intro.author: Paul, with Silvanus (Silas) and Timothy named as co-senders (1:1)
intro.written: About AD 50–51, from Corinth; often considered the earliest of Paul's surviving letters
intro.audience: The young church in Thessalonica, mostly Gentiles who had 'turned to God from idols' (1:9)
intro.setting: Thessalonica was the capital of the Roman province of Macedonia and a busy port on the Via Egnatia, the main road across the region. Paul's stay was cut short when opponents stirred up a mob, and he was sent away by night (Acts 17:1-10). Worried about the new believers, he sent Timothy back from Athens; Timothy returned with good news (3:6), and Paul wrote this letter in response.
intro.purpose: Paul encourages believers facing persecution, recalls his sincere conduct among them, urges holy living, and comforts them about fellow believers who had died before Christ's return.
intro.bigIdea: Hold fast in faith, love and hope while waiting for the Lord's return.

outline.title: Thanksgiving and Paul's bond with the church
Living to please God and waiting for the Lord

commentary.t: THE FIRST EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS
